ops.statement: A Cartographer subagent dispatched at the reconcile step, given the worktree's absolute path in its dispatch prompt, wrote all its architecture-doc edits (docs/architecture/packets/*.md, index.md, overlays/*.yml, a new decisions/*.md file) to the MAIN CHECKOUT instead of the assigned worktree -- a git-invisible failure (the subagent's final report correctly named the files and content, but git status in the assigned worktree showed nothing, while the main checkout showed the exact claimed diff, uncommitted, on a checkout shared with sibling commanders/the human). Caught only because the dispatching commander independently ran git status in BOTH locations rather than trusting the subagent's self-report. Recovery: capture each file's diff/content before touching anything, revert the main checkout to clean (git checkout -- / rm), re-apply the identical changes to the worktree (git apply / cp), re-verify both ends plus the worktree's own architecture-map checker.
ops.grounding: .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md 2026-07-25 663-grip-g INCIDENT+RECOVERY entry: full diff/status evidence for both the main checkout (git diff --stat showed 3 modified + 1 new file before recovery, git status --porcelain empty after) and the worktree (git status --porcelain empty before recovery, correct 4-file change after; scripts/check_arch_map.py OK both before and after).
ops.bank_reason: First observed instance of this specific failure mode (a dispatched subagent's write landing in the wrong repo root despite an explicit worktree path in its prompt) -- the root cause (why the subagent's own tool calls resolved against the main checkout instead of the stated worktree) was not determined this run, so the right fix (stronger prompt wording vs. a self-verify-write-location step built into the Cartographer skill's own doctrine) isn't yet clear. Needs re-observation on a future Cartographer dispatch to see whether it recurs and whether a specific prompt pattern reliably prevents it, before committing to one fix over the other.
